# The drill register

## What it is

A list of the ways this estate can be recovered, and the date each one last
proved it works. A backup nobody has restored is not a backup, and a rollback
nobody has run is not a rollback. The register is what stops either from being
believed on the strength of a green tick.

Everything between the markers below is generated from the register by
`drills/run.py --docs`, and the weekly run regenerates it. It is not typed.

<!-- generated by drills/run.py --docs. Do not edit between the markers. -->
`drills/register.json` holds 13 entries. 8 have a command. 5 have no
command yet, and each one carries the sentence describing what needs
writing.

| drill | written | what breaks without it |
|---|---|---|
| no-anthropic | yes | Anthropic goes down, suspends the account, or prices us out, and every agent on this estate stops at once |
| rebuild | yes | This Mac dies and the estate has to come back on a new machine |
| estate-bundle-restore | yes | A commit exists only on this Mac and the Mac dies |
| offsite-backup-restore | yes | The prospector data is gone and the offsite copy is the only one left |
| key-escrow-restore | yes | This laptop dies and the two age keys die with it, so every encrypted bundle in the offsite bucket is permanently opaque |
| secret-rotation | no | A credential leaks and has to be replaced before anyone can be told it leaked |
| telegram-delivery | yes | Something breaks at 03:00 and the message never arrives |
| windows-rebuild | no | The laptop dies and the replacement is a Windows machine |
| github-gone | no | GitHub suspends the account, goes down for a day, or the org is deleted |
| cloudflare-gone | no | Cloudflare suspends the account or the Workers platform goes away |
| stripe-gone | no | Stripe freezes the account or terminates the relationship |
| db-integrity | yes | A database quietly loses its indexes, every backup faithfully copies the damage, and the first person to find out is whoever runs the restore |
| recovery-posture | yes | A scheduled job stops running and nothing on this Mac notices, because every other instrument grades the output of a job that got a turn |

Every drill-shaped script under `drills/` and `rebuild/` is either run by an entry above or named in the register's `not_drills` list, so none of them is quietly unrun.
<!-- end generated -->

This block used to be typed by hand and it went stale twice inside two days:
it said six entries and named a `fly-rollback` drill the register had retired,
and after that it said eleven entries when there were thirteen and still called
`telegram-delivery` unwritten after it had been written. Two sessions each fixed
the sentence and neither fixed the reason, so the register is now the only copy
and this page renders it.

## How it runs

The launch agent `ai.estate.drills` fires Mondays at 04:30 and runs the whole
register. Results go to `~/.claude/state/drills.jsonl`, one line per run, and a
summary goes to `ESTATE_BOARD.jsonl`.

**It has now fired once, and it was started deliberately rather than by the
clock.** `launchctl print gui/501/ai.estate.drills` reported `runs = 0` for as
long as the job existed, so on 2026-08-23 it was kicked by hand to find out
whether the scheduled path worked at all. It did: four of the five written
drills passed under launchd and `rebuild` failed for a real reason. The first
run on the clock is Monday 2026-08-24 at 04:30, and until that one lands the
schedule itself is still untested.

Nothing needs to be typed for any of that. The commands below are here so an
agent can use them and so you can see what the machine is doing, not because
the register needs a person.

    drills/run.py --list     what is registered and when each last passed
    drills/run.py --all      run everything now
    drills/run.py --check    exit 1 if a drill is failing or has gone stale

## How to turn it off

    launchctl bootout gui/501/ai.estate.drills

That stops the weekly run and nothing else. The register and its history stay on
disk, and `drills/run.py --list` still reports the last known state of each path.
To bring it back, `launchctl bootstrap gui/501 ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.estate.drills.plist`.

## Why NOT WRITTEN does not make it red

A drill with no command yet is counted and named in every report, but it does
not fail the check. A gate that is red forever gets ignored, and an ignored gate
is worse than none, because the next person reads a red board and assumes it has
always been red. The pressure to write the missing four comes from the count
leading every board line, not from a permanent failure.
